name: Question 14
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =2$ and $\sigma =\sqrt{25}=5.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.65<X<-0.25) & =P(\frac{-0.65-2}{5}<Z<\frac{-0.25-2}{5}) \\  & =P(-0.53<Z<-0.45)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/3d73cc4661eb9f68f636803918b3e55942e6538e4e70d13277d125386dad257e.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<-0.45) & =P(Z<-0.45)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.45)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =Φ(-0.45)-Φ(-0.53)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.53) & =0.2981 \\ Φ(-0.45) & =0.3264\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<-0.45) & =Φ(-0.45)-Φ(-0.53) \\  & =0.3264-0.2981 \\  & =0.0283.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-0.65<X<-0.25)=0.0283.
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a normal random variable X∼N(μ,σ2), we have

P(a<X<b)=P(a−μσ<Z<b−μσ)

where Z∼N(0,1) is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have μ=2 and σ=25=5.

First, we transform X into a standard normal random variable Z by z-scoring:

P(−0.65<X<−0.25)=P(−0.65−25<Z<−0.25−25)=P(−0.53<Z<−0.45)

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(−0.53<Z<−0.45)=P(Z<−0.45)−P(Z≤−0.53)=P(Z≤−0.45)−P(Z≤−0.53)=Φ(−0.45)−Φ(−0.53)

From the table, we have the following:

Φ(−0.53)=0.2981Φ(−0.45)=0.3264

Therefore, we have

P(−0.53<Z<−0.45)=Φ(−0.45)−Φ(−0.53)=0.3264−0.2981=0.0283.

Finally, we conclude that

P(−0.65<X<−0.25)=0.0283.
